summary: Iteration 10 (Kasse visibility extended to cashbox recipients) — Backend 6/6 pass, Frontend 3/3 flows verified. GET /api/payments now allows Coach OR any player currently listed as a cashbox recipient_player_id; regular non-recipients receive HTTP 403 with detail 'Nur Trainer und Kassenwarte dürfen Zahlungen einsehen.'. PATCH cascading works: switching bierwart.recipient_player_id from sascha-grins to josh-ankermann grants josh access and revokes sascha's; reset restores the original state. Frontend tabs: Sascha (Bierwart) sees the 'Kasse' tab and lands on the Zahlungen screen with subtitle 'Übersicht aller PayPal-Zahlungen' (no 403 lockout). Filip (regular) has NO Kasse tab. Coach Michael still sees the Kasse tab and full payments overview. Regression: version 3.0 pill count = 1 on login (verified for all three logins).
action_items: OPTIONAL: add a testID to each Tabs.Screen tab bar item (e.g. tab-zahlungen) — currently the only reliable web selector is the anchor href, and 'Kasse' as text collides with the per-event PaypalBierkasseButton on Termine cards.

OPTIONAL: /api/payments already returns previously created test payments (Michael MOSER → Bierwart 0,00 € · Training 3.Sept, status=open). Consider seed cleanup or expose a Coach-only delete endpoint for stale test data.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/routers/cashboxes.py:_can_view_payments — Coach shortcut + recipient_player_id lookup is correct; also implicitly handles Trainer-Kasse recipient (michael-moser) so no double role check needed.

frontend/app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx polls /api/cashboxes once per session but only when player.id or player.position changes. If the Coach reassigns a cashbox while the recipient is already logged in, the newly-added recipient will not see the Kasse tab until they log out and back in (or trigger a screen reload). Not blocking but worth documenting or adding a short interval refresh.

frontend/app/(tabs)/zahlungen.tsx probes via api.listPayments and only shows the 403 lockout after failure; the network call still leaks the actor_id in the URL. This is acceptable for the current threat model.
